events.title: Sinclair ZX80 released
events.summary: Clive Sinclair launched the ZX80 on January 29, 1980 in the UK — a £99 home computer that brought BASIC programming to the mass market.
events.about: The ZX80 shipped with 1 KB RAM and a membrane keyboard but sold in the hundreds of thousands — proving hobbyists would buy cheap programmable machines. Its successor ZX Spectrum defined British game development and bedroom coding culture.

narrative.whyChosen: The ZX80 made home computing affordable outside the US.
narrative.whyImportant: It seeded a generation of European programmers and game developers.
narrative.problemSolved: Personal computers cost thousands; hobbyists needed an entry-level programmable machine.
